newsitem.title: UK: European gasoline cargoes heading to U.S. -traders.
newsitem.headline: European gasoline cargoes heading to U.S. -traders.

text.p: At least 100,000 tonnes of premium unleaded and regular unleaded gasoline are heading for the United States after the arbitrage from Europe opened late last week, traders said on Monday.
But it was unclear if the arbitrage remained open on Monday after cargo and barge prices jumped sharply in Europe and NYMEX futures turned lower, they added.
A 40,000-tonne cargo out of Rotterdam consisting of Eurograde, or premium unleaded, and lower octane gasoline was fixed for the U.S. Atlantic coast, a trader said.
The shipping date was not known but some traders believed it was for prompt delivery.
A 60,000-tonne cargo, also split evenly between premium unleaded and regular, was fixed last Thursday by a U.K. refiner for loading Nov 20, another trader said.
One oil company trader said as many as three or four cargoes were fixed for a total of at least 120,000 tonnes, but this could not be confirmed.
"I think there is still some interest," from the U.S. to buy European cargoes, added another trader.
